openspec-harness:explore.description: Explore business context and risks before creating an OpenSpec change
openspec-harness:explore.template:
Load and follow the skill `openspec-harness-explore` for: $ARGUMENTS

Do not create implementation files. Identify business scenarios, assumptions, open questions, acceptance risks, and likely validation signals. Ensure openspec/harness/test-context.md exists or draft it from the project testing environment. For frontend-visible work, note that later validation must exercise the running application.

openspec-harness:propose.description: Create OpenSpec proposal artifacts for a change
openspec-harness:propose.template:
Load and follow the skill `openspec-harness-propose` for: $ARGUMENTS

Create or update proposal.md, design.md when needed, test.md, tasks.md, and delta specs. Define task-level Test lines and the change-level test plan inside proposal work. Do not ask the user to run a separate testing workflow. Do not start implementation until business, optional design, and test review gates are satisfied.

openspec-harness:review.description: Run adversarial business, design, or implementation review
openspec-harness:review.template:
Load and follow the skill `openspec-harness-review` for: $ARGUMENTS

Review as a skeptical reviewer. Support business, design, test, and implementation review modes. Look for wrong business assumptions, missing scenarios, invalid state transitions, weak test plans, implementation drift, and weak validation evidence. Reject frontend-visible implementation reviews that lack running-app browser behavior evidence.

openspec-harness:apply.template:
Load and follow the skill `openspec-harness-apply` for: $ARGUMENTS

Before editing, run the internal apply gate and use its result as the source of truth. Inspect proposal.md, design.md if present, test.md, tasks.md, review artifacts, and relevant specs. design.md is optional; evidence.md is an archive gate, not an apply prerequisite. Implement one coherent task slice at a time and record implementation evidence. Final test execution belongs to /openspec-harness:verify. Do not expose internal runtime details to the user.

openspec-harness:verify.description: Verify an OpenSpec change against harness gates
openspec-harness:verify.template:
Load and follow the skill `openspec-harness-verify` for: $ARGUMENTS

Run the internal verifier and execute or inspect the checks in test.md using test-context.md. Report missing evidence, failed reviews, failed validation, and exact next actions. For frontend-visible changes, verification must require running-app browser behavior evidence. Do not expose internal runtime details to the user.

openspec-harness:archive.template:
Load and follow the skill `openspec-harness-archive` for: $ARGUMENTS

Before running openspec archive, use the OpenSpec Harness verifier. Do not archive if any required gate fails. Do not archive frontend-visible changes without accepted running-app browser behavior evidence.

openspec-harness:status.template:
Load and follow the skill `openspec-harness-status` for: $ARGUMENTS

Run the internal status check. Do not run shell commands for status unless the user explicitly asks for CLI output. Summarize active changes, inferred state, missing artifacts, incomplete tasks, review gates, and next legal transitions. Do not invent blockers beyond verifier results. Do not print raw JSON, stdout, stderr wrapper fields, or internal runtime details.

openspec-harness:doctor.description: Check OpenSpec Harness installation and OpenCode integration
openspec-harness:doctor.template: Run OpenSpec Harness doctor checks. Verify opencode availability, plugin loading assumptions, OpenSpec files, command namespace, and verifier readiness.

openspec-harness:loop.description: Recommend the next legal OpenSpec Harness loop action
openspec-harness:loop.template:
Load and follow the skill `openspec-harness-loop` for: $ARGUMENTS

Run the internal loop recommender as the source of truth. Report the next legal action, blocked gates, and exact user-facing command to run next. Do not invent blockers beyond the loop or verifier result; design.md is optional and evidence.md is an archive gate. Do not expose internal runtime details to the user.

openspec-harness:context-sync.description: Realign project context after user feedback or requirement drift
openspec-harness:context-sync.template:
Load and follow the skill `openspec-harness-context-sync` for: $ARGUMENTS

First call the internal `openspec_harness_context_sync` tool with write=false when available, then use its classification as the baseline. Update context-level documents when appropriate, and recommend whether the active OpenSpec change can continue or must update proposal/design/test artifacts. Do not edit implementation files during context sync.

openspec-harness:docs-sync.description: Check context-level docs against plugin commands, skills, tools, and package metadata
openspec-harness:docs-sync.template:
Load and follow the skill `openspec-harness-docs-sync` for: $ARGUMENTS

First call the internal `openspec_harness_docs_sync` tool when available and use its result as the baseline. Check README, design docs, context docs, opencode commands, skills, plugin tools, and package metadata for drift. Report or repair documentation drift only; do not implement product changes unless explicitly requested.
